title: Knowledge-to-Jailbreak: Investigating Knowledge-driven Jailbreaking Attacks for Large Language Models

problem.claim: Testing the safety of LLMs on specialized domains such as medicine is increasingly important.

gap.claim: Existing general jailbreaking attacks lack professional knowledge-driven attacks and provide insufficient coverage of domain knowledge for testing domain-specific LLM safety.

contributions.claim: The paper proposes the knowledge-to-jailbreak task, which generates jailbreaking attacks from domain knowledge while requiring attack effectiveness and knowledge relevance.
The paper introduces a dataset containing 12,974 knowledge-jailbreak pairs.
The paper fine-tunes a large language model as a jailbreak-generator for producing domain knowledge-specific jailbreaks.

author_reported_evidence.claim: Experiments across 13 domains and 8 target LLMs demonstrate that the jailbreak-generator produces jailbreaks reported as both threatening to target LLMs and relevant to the supplied knowledge.
On an out-of-domain knowledge base, the authors report that generated jailbreaks have harmfulness comparable to those crafted by human experts.
The authors report that data and code are available.

narrative_sequence.summary: LLM use across domains has increased concern about safety in specialized domains.
Existing general jailbreaking attacks face limitations in professional knowledge use and domain-knowledge coverage.
The proposed knowledge-to-jailbreak task generates attacks from domain knowledge with effectiveness and relevance requirements.
A 12,974-pair dataset is collected and used to fine-tune a jailbreak-generator.
The method is evaluated across multiple domains and target LLMs, including an out-of-domain knowledge base.

source_observation.claim: The proposed attacks are generated from domain knowledge and evaluated for both attack effectiveness and knowledge relevance.

interpretation.claim: Domain-specific safety testing may benefit from evaluating harmfulness together with alignment to the relevant professional knowledge.

application.claim: Design domain-specific safety evaluations that pair knowledge-grounded attack generation with separate effectiveness and relevance criteria.

exception.claim: The abstract does not establish whether this approach generalizes beyond the reported domains, target LLMs, or out-of-domain knowledge-base setting.

unknowns: The abstract does not specify the 13 domains or 8 target LLMs.
The abstract does not describe dataset construction, training details, evaluation metrics, baselines, or statistical results.
The abstract does not define how harmfulness, threat, knowledge relevance, or comparability were measured.
